content:
The test image shows a field-level view with some soybean plants remaining green (stems and leaves retained) while surrounding plants have fully matured and turned brown/tan. This is a whole_plant view. The key feature is the stark contrast between green, leafy plants and senesced neighbors.

Top candidate: **Green_stem_disorder**. Let me verify with reference images across multiple classes.
Strong match - green stem and leaves persisting among mature brown plants. Let me check other candidates.
Not a match - BPMV shows leaf mottling/puckering at close range. The test image is a field-level view of delayed senescence. Let me check more candidates.
SDS shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis across the field - very different from the test image. Let me check more classes.
SCN shows stunted yellowing plants, not the delayed senescence pattern in the test image. Let me check more classes.
White mold shows fluffy white growth and sclerotia on stems - not matching. Let me check Charcoal Rot and Phytophthora.
Charcoal rot shows wilted, dead plants - very different. Let me check Phytophthora whole plant.
Phytophthora shows dead/dying plants in patches among healthy green ones - the opposite pattern of the test image. Now let me view another Green_stem_disorder reference to confirm.

This confirms the pattern: green stems with mature/dry pods, surrounded by fully senesced brown plants. This matches the test image exactly.

The test image shows:
- A field where most plants have matured and turned brown/tan
- A distinct patch/row of plants in the foreground remaining green with retained leaves
- Green stems visible among the otherwise harvest-ready field
- No signs of disease lesions, mold, wilting, or necrosis

This is the hallmark of **Green_stem_disorder**: plants remaining green while neighboring plants have fully senesced. The symptom description states "All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature and senesce" and "stems remain moist and green while pods mature as usual." All 8 reference views used across 8 different classes.

This delayed senescence pattern with green plants among harvest-ready neighbors is the defining characteristic of Green stem disorder. No lesions, mold, wilting, or other disease signs are present."}
